user_query: I want to challenge my father's will. It's unfair.
variations: Will is unfair to me, what can I do?
I think the will was forged
Father was influenced when making his will
part_a_general_info: A will can only be challenged on specific legal grounds: the testator lacked mental capacity (testamentary capacity), was under undue influence, or the will was forged or not properly executed. Unfairness alone is generally not grounds for challenging a will. A person is free to distribute their assets as they wish. However, under the Inheritance (Family Provision) Act, a dependent (spouse, daughter, infant son, or incapacitated child) may apply to the court for reasonable maintenance from the estate if not adequately provided for.
triage_questions: Q1: What is your relationship to the deceased?
Q2: On what grounds do you wish to challenge the will (mental capacity, undue influence, forgery)?
Q3: Do you have evidence supporting your challenge?
Q4: Are you a dependent of the deceased?
branching_logic: If Q2 = 'unfairness' only → Explain this is generally insufficient. Check if Inheritance (Family Provision) Act applies.
If Q2 = undue influence or mental capacity → Will need evidence. Complex litigation.
If Q4 = dependent → May have claim under Inheritance (Family Provision) Act.
routing: Route A (Valid legal grounds): Refer to PBSG clinic. Will likely need private solicitor for contested probate.
Route B (Dependent, inadequate provision): Refer to PBSG clinic for assessment under Inheritance (Family Provision) Act.
Route C (No legal grounds): Inform that unfairness alone is insufficient. Offer referral to PBSG clinic for a second assessment.
guardrail: Must NOT assess the strength of the challenge or advise on litigation strategy.
